result.rule: When the description states a chain of activities in which each sentence introduces the next activity, some phrased passively or as a hand-off to another party, and then a party records one of two outcomes that either sends the work back to an earlier party or lets the process continue.: Model every stated activity in the chain, including passive or hand-off activities, as its own task in sequence, placed in the lane of the party that performs it. Model the checking step as its own task performed by the party that records the outcome, placed after the last task of the chain and before an exclusive gateway. Give that gateway one conditioned outgoing flow per outcome. On the return branch, model the stated return as its own task performed by the party named in the description, and connect it back to the earlier stated activity so the loop is visible. On the continuation branch, model the stated continuation as a task or as a flow into the next activity, and do not replace it with an end event unless the description says the process ends there.

When the description states that a participant checks a request received from another participant, and then gives a reply whose content depends on the result of that check, so that the reply is one of several stated alternatives: Model the check as a task performed by the checking participant. Model the reply as a separate task performed by that same participant, placed after the check task and not merged into it or dropped. When the reply depends on the check result, place an exclusive gateway after the check task, with one conditioned outgoing flow per stated alternative, each leading to the activity that produces that alternative. Close each branch with an end event after its activity, so that the reply is modeled and no outcome is left without an end.

When the description states that, after a completing step is finished, a further action follows it (for example, a participant is configured or enabled), and the process ends with that further action together with another outcome: Model each stated follow-up action as its own task placed after the completing task and connected to it by a sequence flow, in the order the description gives. Connect that task to the end event or to the final task so the action is not skipped, and do not fold it into the completing task or the final task.
